A.summary: Two large modules: spec.py normalises dict records through long hand-written validators and a closed four-way type switch, and registry.py holds lookup, binding, refusal building, confirmation and the walk inline. Consumers are pure functions in schema.py, but the binder is lenient: it rewrites redirected and case-mismatched names instead of refusing them.

host decides confirmation: the host set is ORed with the record flag in run and in tool_schema/help, impl-A/hubreg/registry.py:455-461,523
forces_in_tension: strictness against forgiveness: tipped to forgiveness. Option redirects and case-insensitive matches are rewritten and bound with only a REDIRECT warning (impl-A/hubreg/registry.py:280-298), action redirects are followed (impl-A/hubreg/registry.py:193-198), and a bare name resolves across device kinds when unique (impl-A/hubreg/registry.py:168-170). The chapter's 'refuse with a fix' is not followed

A.best_thing: Effective confirmation (host set OR record flag) is computed once and passed to every consumer: run, tool_schema and help (impl-A/hubreg/registry.py:455-461, 520-534).
A.worst_thing: The binder rewrites near-miss names (redirect, case-insensitive, cross-kind bare name) instead of refusing with a fix, so the hub can run an action the caller did not name.

generativity.notes: B, C and E share a deep structure (record, ArgType, binder, diagnoser, describer, walker, finalize, hook) that differs in detail. B keeps the type table per registry with a limits_apply flag and a walker that generates negative probes. C puts enum membership inside accepts and dispatches Failure through a handler table. E puts limits on the type (range_problem) and indexes action redirects. All three still special-case 'number'/'enum' outside the type objects, and two of them (C, E) made the type table global. A and D have a monolithic Registry with a closed type switch. They differ on the strictness force: A rewrites near-misses, while D refuses with advisory hints and extends redirects to enum values.

worse_is_better: D is the smallest (about 1700 source lines against about 2100 for the others). It reaches the same refusal quality as B, C and E on unknown names, limits, defaults and host confirmation, without a Failure type, finalize, hook or type objects. For the current four types that is enough. What the B/C/E group carries beyond D is justified by the task's own next change: the ArgType seam turns the rgb type into a new file instead of edits to three core files. A separate diagnoser is the extra most worth having. Extras that no requirement needs: B's internal flag, callable fields and allow_forward_redirects, C's unused render() duty and Record.raw, E's surfaces.py, and the validate hook in all three, which no record uses. A carries the most code for the least resolution: lenient name rewriting and validators written out by hand.
chapter_lessons: Flags resolved by host policy must reach the describers, not only run(). B and C compute effective confirmation in run but render tool schema/help from the plug-in flag (impl-B/hubreg/describe.py:164, impl-C/hubreg/describe.py:235). The Structure should say the registry answers 'needs confirmation?' and every consumer asks it.

The ArgType interface in note 6 (accept, check, describe) is too small. Every implementation with pluggable types still switches on 'number'/'enum' to decide which spec keys apply (limits, values), to build repair examples and to coerce CLI input (impl-C/hubreg/record.py:317, impl-E/hubreg/record.py:194, impl-B/hubreg/diagnoser.py:261, impl-E/hubreg/diagnose.py:194). The chapter should add 'validate spec keys', 'example/alternatives for repairs' and 'parse from text'.
Say where the type table lives. C and E made it module-global, so types leak between registries and tests; B's per-registry table is the safer default.

'Redirect' invites rewriting. A followed redirects and case-insensitive matches silently (impl-A/hubreg/registry.py:280-298). The Solution and Sketch, not only note 8, should state that a redirect only produces a refusal with a fix.

Mark optional participants as optional. The validate hook, callable fields and the internal flag were built with no record to use them (impl-B/hubreg/records.py:44,211). The Structure table reads as a checklist.
Say where the result check lives (run or walker). C checks it in both, leaving dead walker code (impl-C/hubreg/walker.py:107-120); E and B check it only in the walker.
Note 9 was misread as covering CLI subcommands (impl-E/hubreg/surfaces.py). Clarify that 'reachable from the agent' means callable operations, not the tool's own command line.
